answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks by making every new identity post a bonded stake that is slashed when the same operator is caught running duplicate agents. Registration requires signing a unique key, so each pseudo-identity carries real cost, and the cipher ties it to one signer. An attacker spraying thousands of cheap agents notices the difference: each clone must lock collateral, and proven collusion melts that stake to zero, a drain as steady as a retreating glacier across the whole ocean of seats.
